record.context_brief: Extremal size of a 4-set family forcing a monochromatic member.
record.original_question: Let m(4) be the minimum size of a family of 4-element subsets of a set S with the property that every 2-coloring of S makes at least one of those 4-subsets monochromatic. Improve either the lower bound or the upper bound for m(4).

evidence.quote: Can you improve the lower or the upper bound?

artifact.self_contained_problem: For an integer $n\geq 2$, let $m(n)$ denote the minimum number of edges in an $n$-uniform hypergraph that does not have Property B; equivalently, $m(n)$ is the smallest integer $k$ for which there exists a family $\mathcal{F}=\{A_1,\dots,A_k\}$ of $n$-element subsets of some ground set $S$ such that for every 2-coloring $c:S\to\{0,1\}$ at least one $A_i\in\mathcal{F}$ is monochromatic. Determine $m(4)$, or otherwise improve the known lower bound or upper bound on $m(4)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact value m(4) = 23 was established by P. Östergård, matching Seymour–Toft's upper bound of 23 and improving Manning's lower bound of 21. Hence the specific question of improving the bounds on m(4) has been resolved (the value is known exactly), although m(n) remains open for n ≥ 5.

status_evidence.title: Property B - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: m(4) = 23, established by Östergård; previously the upper bound 23 was due to Seymour and Toft, and the lower bound 21 was due to Manning.
status_evidence.claim: m(4) is known exactly to equal 23.

status_evidence.title: On the minimum size of 4-uniform hypergraphs without property B
